items.statement: The adjacent complete theorem derives polynomial ridge L2 membership and an exact direction-independent norm from actual standard Gaussian and unit-weight inputs. The common positive bound depends on the polynomial alone.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space; its measurable structure is Borel.
p is any finite real polynomial. The Gaussian measures are actual standard Gaussian laws, and feature weights range over the literal unit-norm subtype.

formulae.label: actual Gaussian projection and ridge isometry

obligations.label: Polynomial Gaussian ridges have one dimension-independent L2 norm

bindings.boundary: The Gaussian law and unit norm are essential. This is not a theorem for arbitrary rotation-invariant heavy-tailed laws or unbounded directions.; No pointwise feature bound is claimed. No label moment, averaging over arbitrary parameter laws, global risk first variation or stochastic convergence is supplied.

assumption_deltas.source: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, and p any real polynomial. Put phi(z)=p(z), gamma1=N(0,1), gammaE=stdGaussian(E), and U={w in E: norm(w)=1}. Then phi genuinely belongs to L2(gamma1). Define b=norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)}+1. One has b>0, and every actual ridge x↦phi(<w,x>) for w in U genuinely belongs to L2(gammaE), with norm exactly norm(phi)_{L2(gamma1)} and hence at most b. The one base norm and the same b serve every direction and dimension. Neither positive dimension, a nonzero polynomial nor evenness is required; the feature conclusions are vacuous when U is empty. No feature moment, covariance or uniform bound is assumed.
assumption_deltas.lean: The full adjacent signature has exactly the displayed actual Gaussian measures, finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel structure, finite polynomial and unit-weight subtype. L2 membership, equality and the bound are conclusions.
assumption_deltas.reason: No feature moment or bound producer is turned into a premise. No nonzero polynomial or positive-dimension restriction is added.
